mgk-niac-cover.png

museum/public/held/robots/art/mgk-niac-cover.png
size
604 KB · 1200 × 1200 · png
used by
src/data/artists/robots.js
what it is
The MGK-NIAC album cover — the house ROBOTS template with the machine's own head, lens forward, set into the disc the WB mark used to occupy, and the model number where the word ROBOTS was.
Ops on quality
THE FURNITURE IS EXACT AND THE BADGE IS THE WHOLE CABINET. Every constant is lifted from tools/make_robots_cover.py, so the ground, the border, the setting, the rule and the strapline are the front desk's own to the pixel. [K1 2026-08-07] THIS NOTE WAS THREE ROUNDS STALE AND NAMED A FILE THAT NO LONGER EXISTS — it described the head_lens.jpg badge and the argument that the museum held no photograph of this machine whole. Both were overtaken: R4 swapped the badge to core_helical.jpg, P7 swapped it again to cabinet_whole.jpg, which IS the first photograph of the mainframe whole, and D5 made it ride the ring as a plate rather than a cut-out because the frame is cropped at the cabinet's own bounding box and has no room in it to matte away. head_lens.jpg was deleted with the other ten operator plates at K1. The badge is 858x1438 fitted whole into the disc's inscribed box (focal = None), so the paper shows in the disc's corners by design and nothing of the machine is cropped away. Register P4 — a frame with air around the object, which is what a true cut-out would need — is still open and is a photograph Mike brings.
Preview shown at up to 1000px on the long edge, flattened onto white. Judge the file, not the preview, if it is close.

mgk-viiip-cover.png

museum/public/held/robots/art/mgk-viiip-cover.png
size
445 KB · 1200 × 1200 · png
used by
src/data/artists/robots.js
what it is
The MGK-VIIIp album cover — the house ROBOTS template with the whole unit in the disc and the model number below it.
Ops on quality
This is the instruction met exactly: front_full.png is the unit, square on, whole, sharp, and the disc crop takes it without cutting the machine. The faceplate and the lit glass are legible inside the badge at full size, which is a bonus rather than the point — at deck size it reads as an object. Two departures from the base cover, both deliberate and both applied to BOTH machine covers so the pair cannot drift: the rule sits 14px lower so this name's descender clears it, and the letter-tracking is solved per cover so nine glyphs set inside the measure six do. The word still runs wider than the rule beneath it, which the six-glyph cover does not — the one place the pair is visibly unequal.
Preview shown at up to 1000px on the long edge, flattened onto white. Judge the file, not the preview, if it is close.

core_helical.jpg

museum/public/held/robots/reference/mgk-viii/core_helical.jpg
size
92 KB · 380 × 820 · jpg
used by
src/data/artists/robots.js
what it is
MGK-NIAC plate 1 of 4, and the album cover's badge — the helical core through the cage bars.
Ops on quality
THE ONE UNMISTAKABLE FEATURE OF THE MAINFRAME, and the reason it is the cover: a blue coil down the middle of a cabinet, read through a grid of bars, with the element's warm flanks either side of it. 380x820, so it is a TALL frame and the cover's circular badge takes a square out of it — the crop rides high (focal 0.36) so the disc holds coil rather than the core's foot and the loose cable. Soft, as every frame lifted from 2021 phone video is; at badge size that reads as depth rather than as blur. FOR MIKE: the blue is the whole of what makes this frame, and the wing's B&W law takes it at the glass — the file keeps its colour on disk.
Preview shown at up to 1000px on the long edge, flattened onto white. Judge the file, not the preview, if it is close.

what it is
MGK-NIAC plate 4 of 4, and the album's viewer poster — the interior flooded red-orange.
Ops on quality
THE MOST DRAMATIC FRAME IN THE SET and the one that most looks like a 1965 machine in trouble: the whole cage red, the element glowing through it, the core's helix still legible as a separate blue-white line. 560x740. FOR MIKE, AND IT IS A QUESTION RATHER THAN A DEFECT: the robots repo's own record of this frame calls it the meltdown and quotes you on tape saying so, but nothing in the MUSEUM's fiction says this machine has ever been in trouble. The caption states what the frame shows and stops there. If a fault is part of NIAC's story, this plate is where it starts.

Ops on quality
THE OUTPUT ROW, MID-PATTERN, which is the only frame in either repository showing this machine SAYING something. Two banks of red bar-graph modules behind the bars with a dark square aperture between them; the lit segments are uneven across the banks, which is what makes it read as a readout rather than as a lamp test. 690x240 — a wide letterbox, so it will sit in a collage tile with generous mat above and below and it is the wrong shape for any square slot. It carries the TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS face's own 1 x 64 entry as a picture.
